rationale:
The subject `ValidationContext.read` has two obligations. A successful read must return the node contents. It must also record the fingerprint of the returned contents as a node dependency. The `read_node.inputs` text adds that a failed read records no successful observation. The agent delivery rules in that text belong to the harness, not to `read`, so they are outside this subject.

Both marked tests cover these obligations:

- **`snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions`**
  - After `read(&1)` returns "before", `dependencies()` is exactly `[Node(1, fp("before"))]`. This checks the recorded node identity and the fingerprint of the returned content.
  - After the content changes, `read(&1)` returns "after" and the final dependencies are `[Node(1, fp("before")), Node(1, fp("after"))]`. This checks that a changed fingerprint is recorded as a new observation, and that the `earlier` copy keeps the old observation.
  - `read(&2)` fails with an error and the dependency list is unchanged. The test also checks the underlying `reads` vector `[1,1,1,2]`.
  - The `finish` record carries the same dependencies, and `is_current` is false after the change.
- **`direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots`**
  - It runs over empty content and a large multi-byte Unicode content.
  - `read` returns the complete contents (`contents.format() == original`). The dependencies equal `Node(1, fp(original))`.
  - The returned contents are unaffected by a later graph change.
  - A failed `read(&9)` returns the error "missing" and leaves `dependencies()` empty.

Together these cover the success path, the exact fingerprint of the returned contents, re-reads of changed content, and the failed-read case. The `public_api` test only checks exports and is not needed for this subject. I found no untested obligation or weak assertion, and no marking gap.

text: :::{req} ValidationContext.read
Read a graph node and record the fingerprint of the returned contents under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`.
```rust,ignore
impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D> {
pub fn read(&self, node: &D::NodeId) -> Result<D::NodeContent, D::Error>;
:::{req} read_node.inputs
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
